title: Safe traffic bifurcation with tenant credit demarcation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a production-safe traffic bifurcation system that lets us route a controlled fraction of live requests to test model variants while strictly bounding cost, isolating tenant resources, and providing fast automatic rollback on quality regressions. This ticket covers the end-to-end pipeline: sampling policy, per-tenant credit demarcation, tenant-level isolation when test lanes exceed budget, telemetry hooks, and operator controls for rollout and emergency cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Can route sampled production traffic to a test lane (configurable by percent or deterministic hashed key) with per-tenant credit accounting enabled
Per-tenant budget/demarcation prevents test traffic from consuming more than allocated credits; excess requests are either routed to baseline model or dropped to avoid overrun

Automatic rollback trigger: when quality regression metrics (error-rate, hallucination-rate on eval set, latency SLO violations) cross configured thresholds, the pipeline stops routing to the test lane within 60s
Telemetry: request-level metadata (sample_version, sample_bucket, credit_consumed, fallback_reason) emitted to tracing and the console cost dashboard
Integration tests and a staged canary demonstrate safe behavior on a subset of tenants before full enablement
design_notes: Use deterministic hash-based bucketing on (tenant_id, request_id, user_id) to allow reproducible sampling and easy offline repros
Introduce a lightweight credit-demarcation ledger per tenant used only by the bifurcation controller; ledger entries expire after 24h and are reconciled asynchronously to accounting
When a tenant's test-lane credit is exhausted, requests should be routed to the baseline model with a fallback_reason tag (credit_exhausted) rather than queued, to keep latency predictable
Sampling policies: support fixed-rate percentage, adaptive budget-based sampling (tokens per minute), and stratified sampling for high-value tenants
Fail-open vs fail-closed: by default pipeline will fail-open to baseline model on controller errors, but ops can flip to fail-closed during incidents
Cost control levers: per-tenant max-TPM, global test-lane cap, and low-cost surrogate model option for heavy requests
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature flag gated locally; unit and integration tests against mock ledger and mock models
Phase 2 (internal): enable for Redwood internal tenants only (canary group), observe accounting and false-positive rates for 48h
Phase 3 (partner): opt-in customers with > fair-usage SLA; enable conservative sampling (0.1% or small fixed credit), run for 1 week
Phase 4 (general availability): default off for new tenants, opt-in + guided console flow for enablement; automated alerts and one-click rollback in console
metrics: fallback_rate (percent of sampled requests that fell back to baseline) by reason
latency_p50/p95 for sampled vs baseline lanes
monitoring: Add traces: bifurcation.controller.*, bifurcation.ledger.* with sample_version and credit_consumed fields
Dashboard card: per-tenant test-lane burn rate with predicted days-to-exhaustion based on moving average
Scheduled job: daily ledger reconciliation report and anomaly detector for unexpected credit drains
Pager rule: if rollback_trigger fires for >3 tenants in 5m, page SRE
testing: Unit tests for hash bucketing and deterministic behavior across SDK language bindings
Integration test with model-mock that asserts fallback behaviour when ledger reports exhausted
Chaos test: simulate controller lag and ensure fail-open routes to baseline within 2s
Performance test: end-to-end latency impact for high-throughput tenant (target <5ms added p50)
E2E canary run with synthetic traffic and eval prompt set to verify rollback semantics

2025-04-25 QA (Jordan Li): Found race where simultaneous ledger writes for same tenant can double-count during controller retry. Added optimistic compare-and-swap and compensating reconcile job in testing plan.
